assumptions.data: Synthetic scripted orders and iid random limit orders; no market data
assumptions.price_unit: integer ticks with unit tick value
assumptions.random_order_distribution: buy/sell equiprobable; prices 95..105, sizes 1..9, owners 0..7 uniform

assumptions.data: Synthetic; independent pre-generated external paths shared by policies
assumptions.arrival: Reference midpoint before first external event
assumptions.liquidity: Five levels per side, 10 units each, mid +/-3..7; fully refreshed every batch
assumptions.event_order: Refresh background, external IOC, parent IOC; no resting parent remainder
assumptions.shortfall: s*(notional-filled*arrival) + fees + s*residual*(terminal_mid-arrival); s=+1 buy, -1 sell
assumptions.residual: Unexecuted positive parent units; marked at terminal reference, not liquidated
assumptions.baseline: Release entire parent at batch zero and retry residual every batch
assumptions.twap: Cumulative floor(Q*(t+1)/T) target each batch; carry deficits, no forced terminal fill
assumptions.uncertainty: 16 independent paired seeds 200..215; Student t(15) 95% CI for TWAP minus baseline; negative favors TWAP
assumptions.boundaries: No calibrated flow, permanent impact, latency, funding, borrow cost, hidden depth, or fee tiers

provenance.data: Synthetic Gaussian midprice moves and distance-dependent arrivals; separate synthetic order-book scenarios

limitations: Legacy policy metrics still use the quote-arrival model, independently of the new order book.
Order book is a single-instrument limit-order model without cancellation, amendments, auctions, hidden liquidity, latency, or self-trade prevention.
No calibrated adverse-selection, market-impact, or endogenous order-flow model.
Order-book accounting assumes zero fees/costs and unlimited credit/shorting; legacy simulator charges 0.001 per filled unit.
Terminal inventory is marked at mid without liquidation costs; simulated PnL is not evidence of tradability.
